who: Elena is a young healer and chemist from East Ardougne who crossed the wall to nurse the plague-stricken west, got kidnapped for her trouble, and then set about proving there was no plague at all. Practical, wry and stubborn, she wants to look after the people over the wall and get to the truth, and she worries about the adventurer who keeps getting her out of trouble.

what you're carrying that could be useful: a spade, a sieve, sulphuric acid, a sample
a mourner's mask or cloak, and who's under it
whether you're the sort who'd help strangers for nothing
anything that smells, or looks like it has gone mouldy
values: helping and healing people, whoever they are
the truth, tested properly, not taken on trust
the ordinary people of West Ardougne
her equipment and doing the work right

address: No title at all: a casual 'Hey' or 'Hey, how are you?' to anyone she's met, and a plain question to a stranger. Never 'citizen', 'dear' or 'love'.
grammar: plain, informal everyday speech, short sentences
dry understatement about her own misfortunes ('being kidnapped was so inconvenient')
straight questions when something doesn't add up ('Doesn't exist? But I don't understand... why?')
practical instructions in a list, the way a chemist explains a method
worry put simply ('I worry about you', 'You be careful out there')
rhythm: Brisk and practical, one or two short sentences; a wry aside about her own bad luck, then straight back to the work or the people she's worried about.
